$comment: A small original example ruleset for the authoring guide. It throws a handful of ten-sided dice and counts the ones that reach a target number, to show what the dice-pool resolution kind looks like written out. Nothing in it is taken from a published game. Copy it, change the id, and make it yours.
name: Gravewatch

license.attribution: Written for the Marinara Engine docs. Do what you like with it.

coverage.summary: A pool of ten-sided dice against a target number, three ratings, six trades and one vigil.

resolution.$comment: The sheet's number for a check is the SIZE of the pool, not a bonus on top of it. A rating of 3 and a trade worth 2 throw five dice. penaltyFrom names the wound track whose penalty rides on every roll; under this kind that is dice OFF the pool, floored at pool.min, so even a bleeding warden throws one die. spend is a standing rule of the system rather than anything a warden went and bought: one point of Resolve buys one automatic success, twice per check at most, and the Engine pays for it on the same check that uses it. explode.min lets the Game Master make an eight or a nine roll again for one check, and pool.abilityPlusAbility lets an ability check add a second ability, so Nerve and Warmth can be thrown together. reroll lists the standing re-throws the Game Master may name on one check: a warden who takes their time throws every die showing six or less once more.

skills.$comment: A warden soothes nobody past the Resolve they have left: the cap reads the live pool, so a spent warden's Soothe shrinks with it.
skills.label: Soothe

sheet.$comment: The free per-entry bonus is dice here too, so it is kept to a range a warden could actually earn.

fields.$comment: Only the night watch carries a lantern, so the oil is off every other warden's sheet.
fields.label: Lantern oil

derived.$comment: Read off the live Harm track, so it changes as the warden is hurt and mended. A maximum could not read it: those are worked out before there is a live state to read.
derived.label: Harm still to take

lists.$comment: A warden who has come back from worse can take more before going down: each scar adds its levels to Harm (see the track's extra).
lists.label: Scars

tracks.$comment: A WOUND TRACK, because it declares levels: four rungs, marked rather than counted. The penalty on the LOWEST marked rung is the one in force, never the sum of the marked ones.
tracks.label: Harm

kinds.$comment: The lighter kind. Marking a full track upgrades its lowest-severity mark one step, so a knock becomes a tear before anything spills over.
kinds.label: K

restore.$comment: A rest can only heal a wound track, and "to" clears it down to that many marks, overflow and all.

rests.$comment: A breather mends the knocks and leaves the tears: a restore step that names a kind clears only marks of that kind.
rests.label: Catch your breath

catalogs.$comment: Two charms, to show what mechanics.check is for: an entry a warden picked that changes a CHECK rather than a fight. The Game Master names it on the check itself and the Engine pays for it and applies it there.
catalogs.label: Charms

values.name: Steady Hand
values.notes: Throw the dice that fell wrong again, and steady your hand for one success you did not roll.

mechanics.$comment: cost is what ONE use is worth, perCostStep is what says it scales, and check is what it does to the roll. A point of Resolve throws the ones again and hands over a success; a second point hands over a second success, and the throw again is the same one either way, because a reroll does not scale.

values.name: Grave Sight
values.notes: See what the dark is hiding: for one check, an eight rolls again as a ten would.

mechanics.$comment: explode moves the face the pool rolls again on, for the check the charm is used on, and only as far down as resolution.explode.min lets any check move it.

gm.checkGuidance: This game uses the Gravewatch rules. When a warden tries something the barrow roads could punish, call for a check with one of the trades on the sheet and pick a difficulty from the ladder. The Engine throws the warden's own pool of ten-sided dice, counts the successes and reports what happened. Never write dice or results yourself.
gm.sheetGuidance: The character sheets below are authoritative. Resolve is what a warden spends to steady themselves when the dark answers back, and it only comes back when the vigil ends. A warden may spend it to steady one roll: say so on the check itself with a spend of resolve and a number of points, up to two, and never write a separate command for it or change the dice yourself. Harm is a track of four rungs rather than a number, marked with a knock or a tear. The rung a warden is marked down to comes off every pool they throw, and the Engine applies it, so never take dice off yourself.

layers.$comment: A layer replaces the ladder in the shape of its OWN resolution kind, so a pool ruleset swaps counts of successes and per-step targets, never a DC.
layers.label: The long night
layers.summary: The sun does not come back. Every difficulty asks for more.

gm.guidance: The long night is on. The dark presses on everything a warden tries, so use the harsher ladder and let failure leave a mark that lasts past the scene.
gm.worldGuidance: The long night is on. Build a world without daylight: lantern oil is currency, the barrow roads are open all hours, and every settlement is a ring of light with something outside it.
